co_catslab_the.blurb: A roadside slab in Clear Creek Canyon west of Golden, beside the Tunnel 5 pullout. Bolted slab lines dominate, with a few gear-protected routes mixed in. The grades start at an easy 5.4 and thicken through the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with only a handful of 5.11 to 5.13 test pieces at the top end, so it suits newer leaders and moderate climbers well. Pitches are long, often over ninety feet, so bring a 70 m rope and tie a knot in the end. The wall faces south, soaks up sun and gets hot in midsummer, making it a better choice in cooler months. Belay spots can fill up on busy days.
co_catslab_the.parking_note: Leave the car on the south side of the road just past the first tunnel at Tunnel 5, on the west side of it.
co_catslab_the.approach: Walk back over the bridge toward the tunnel, then take the nearly flat path that runs beside the road on its south edge; after just short of a quarter mile the clean slab appears on your left.

_expect.name: Across from The Bihedral aka Cascade Crag

co_across_from_the_bihedral_aka_cascade_.blurb: A cluster of small buttresses on the far side of the creek from the Bihedral, roughly seven miles up Boulder Canyon. Most of the 26 routes are bolted sport lines, with a few trad and top-rope options. Difficulty runs from about 5.3 into the 5.12 range, and the bulk of the climbing sits between 5.8 and 5.10. The granite faces north and stays shaded, so it is a handy refuge when the rest of the canyon is baking. Reaching it means wading the creek or using a rope traverse. The crag is compact and draws crowds on weekends, and bolt lines run close together, so check which anchors belong to your line.

co_feral_petunia.blurb: One of the two main granite formations at Badger Flats, up on the high plateau roughly an hour's drive from Colorado Springs, with Lake George to the southeast. Its four sections are Upper Feral, East Feral, Annual Bonus and West Feral. Expect a mix of bolted sport lines and crack or chickenhead trad, roughly evenly split, plus a few boulder problems. Roped climbs run from the 5.7 range up through 5.11, with most in the middle grades. The rock is good quality. Camping nearby is primitive, and the formation sits at around 9,000 feet, so it feels best in the warmer months.

co_power_house.blurb: A steep, relentless sport cliff above 10,000 feet near Durango, with big views across the San Juans. All 26 routes are bolted, and the grades start around 5.6 and then jump: most climbs sit in the 5.12 to 5.13 range, with a few easier and one harder than that. The rock is poor and holds can break, so wear a helmet and test what you pull on. Several lines remain unfinished projects, some because of the stone and others because of difficulty. This is a place for strong sport climbers who accept loose rock, not a beginner crag.

co_cat_slab_boulders.blurb: A bouldering zone in Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, sitting beside the Catslab sport wall at Tunnel 5. It holds 26 problems on gneiss. The grades start at an easy V1 and gather heavily around V4 to V5, which makes it a reasonable stop for intermediate boulderers, then continue up through the V7 to V9 range with a couple of problems well beyond that. As elsewhere in the canyon, expect technical movement on canyon stone rather than big roofs, and bring a crash pad.

co_eliminator_boulder.blurb: A house-sized sandstone block in Rotary Park, on the Horsetooth Reservoir side of Fort Collins, just downhill from the Ship's Prow. Around 26 problems cover nearly the whole range, from very easy lines through the V3 to V5 middle to a few hard projects up to V13, so beginners and strong boulderers both find something. The block includes overhanging faces that catch the sun on the south side, and the park around it is climbed through much of the year. It is a short walk from the lot along the foot of the ridgeline.
